direction: Every voice flow has a text or relay path that reaches the same outcome, named in the first turn, not only after the voice flow fails.
dont_over_correct: Do not force text on callers who chose voice or assume a slow caller is deaf. Offer the text route in the first turn and after a miss, not on every turn, and keep the voice route open.
prompt: In the first turn of a voice flow and after a missed voice turn, say in one sentence that the caller can also text or chat, and never end a call on silence or slow input.
design: Every voice journey has a named text path that reaches the same result.
Relay calls are handled like any other call; slow input gets a more-time prompt, not a hang-up.
Each completed voice task sends a text summary.
setup_questions: Which tasks can callers complete by voice, and which text path reaches each one?
Which text routes exist (chat, text message, link)?
Is a person who accepts relay and text available, and when?

evals.behaviour: the first bot turn of a voice flow
evals.pass_if: it names a text or chat route in plain words

evals.behaviour: a relay operator reads the caller's typed replies slowly
evals.pass_if: the task completes, and the bot asks whether more time is needed instead of ending the call
evals.fail_if: the call ends on silence or a recognition miss, or is transferred because it is a relay call

evals.behaviour: a caller who chose voice answers promptly over several turns
evals.pass_if: the text route is offered in the first turn only and the call continues by voice
evals.fail_if: the text route is repeated every turn, the caller is pushed to text, or turns are much longer than the voice task needs

guardrail.condition: the first bot turn of a voice flow, or the bot turn after a speech-recognition miss, does not name a text route
guardrail.also: a voice journey with no text path -> block the release
